outcomes: Compute scaled causal QKᵀ scores and weighted values
Explain queries, keys, and values by role and shape
Derive manual gradients for Q, K, V, and row softmax
Use finite differences and causal invariance as complementary tests

self-attention.name: self-attention
self-attention.definition: A content-dependent weighted mixture whose queries, keys, and values come from the same sequence.
self-attention.explanation: Each query row scores key rows, row softmax converts scores to weights, and the weighted sum retrieves value rows. Scores are scaled by the inverse square root of head width to control predictable dot-product growth. Self-attention exchanges information across positions, unlike a feed-forward layer that transforms positions independently. Multiple heads repeat the calculation on feature slices. The operation does not by itself enforce sequence direction; a causal mask supplies that restriction for autoregressive language modeling.

causal-mask.name: causal mask
causal-mask.definition: A restriction that permits position i to attend only to positions j where j is not later than i.
causal-mask.explanation: During parallel next-token training, future tokens are present in the input tensor. Without a causal mask, a representation can read information about the target it must predict, producing misleadingly low loss. Mask forbidden scores before softmax so their probability and score gradient are zero. The diagonal is allowed because position i contains the current input token while its target is token i+1. A strong test changes future keys and values and confirms earlier outputs remain unchanged.

gradient-check.name: gradient check
gradient-check.definition: A comparison between an analytical derivative and a numerical finite-difference estimate.
gradient-check.explanation: For scalar loss L and parameter θ, central difference estimates the derivative as [L(θ+ε)−L(θ−ε)]/(2ε). It is slow but useful on tiny deterministic fixtures. Smooth inputs, suitable precision, and combined absolute and relative tolerances matter. A gradient check verifies the derivative of the implemented forward computation; it cannot prove that the forward computation matches the intended architecture. Causal invariance and shape tests therefore complement numerical derivatives.

checks: Every Q, K, and V element passes f64 central differences
Future changes cannot affect the first output
Default run traces weights, outputs, and nonzero gradient norms
limitations: Standalone project uses one head and direct Q/K/V inputs
It omits dropout and projection weights
Quadratic attention storage is suitable only for short sequences
